data.title: Phase 3 RAINIER Results Supporting Best-in-Class Potential of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy Published in the New England Journal of Medicine and Presented at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2026
data.description:
Phase 3 RAINIER Results Supporting Best-in-Class Potential of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy Published in the New England Journal of Medicine and Presented at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2026

- Vertex is on track for the U.S. FDA Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of November 30 for potential accelerated approval of povetacicept –

- Data published in NEJM and presented at ASN highlight povetacicept’s unique trifecta of efficacy, favorable safety, and the simplicity of dosing at-home every 4 weeks with a low-volume autoinjector –

- Data presented at ASN include a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on current and emerging IgAN therapies, showing that 96% of participants preferred an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, and 80% of participants preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing -

- New clinical studies of povetacicept underway including a study evaluating patient experience on povetacicept administered via autoinjector -

Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (Nasdaq: VRTX) today announced the publication of Phase 3 RAINIER results for povetacicept in the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM), presentation of these data at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado, and advancement of the povetacicept clinical research program in IgAN. Vertex will also host an investor event during ASN on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT). Further details are below.

Data being presented include a pre-specified Week 36 interim analysis of the ongoing Phase 3 RAINIER trial of povetacicept, an engineered fusion protein and dual inhibitor of the BAFF (B cell activating factor) and APRIL (a proliferation inducing ligand) cytokines, in immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). RAINIER met its primary endpoint, with povetacicept achieving a 52.0% reduction from baseline in proteinuria at Week 36 and a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001), while also meeting both secondary endpoints.

The Week 36 interim analysis of RAINIER demonstrated that the depth of proteinuria reduction from baseline was consistent across demographic, clinical and regional subgroups, including an unprecedented 54.2% reduction in urine protein to creatinine ratio (UPCR) versus placebo in North America. Additionally, findings showed that 42.2% of povetacicept-treated participants reached 24-hour UPCR <0.5 g/g, the threshold aligned with current Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines, compared with only 6.2% on placebo. Importantly, these findings were observed on top of optimized supportive care in both treatment arms, including sodium-glucose co-transporter 2(SGLT2) inhibitor use in 65.8% of participants, which is among the highest reported of any contemporary IgAN trial.

“At just 36 weeks of treatment, povetacicept has delivered impressive efficacy results, together with favorable safety and convenient dosing at-home every 4 weeks in a low-volume auto-injector that can fit into the lives of IgAN patients, underscoring the potential of povetacicept to substantially impact and redefine expectations for disease control in IgAN,” said Carmen Bozic, M.D., Executive Vice President, Global Medicines Development and Medical Affairs, and Chief Medical Officer at Vertex. “We are grateful to the patients, investigators, and study teams who made RAINIER the largest and fastest-enrolling contemporary IgAN trial to date and look forward to the November 30th PDUFA target action date.”

“What stands out from the RAINIER results is the important clinical validation of simultaneously targeting BAFF and APRIL to address upstream drivers and kidney injury in IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept was specifically designed as a high-potency, high-affinity TACI fusion protein with broad tissue distribution to deliver this dual inhibition in order to target upstream pathogenic immune complex production,” said Richard Lafayette, M.D., Professor of Medicine (Nephrology) at Stanford University Medical Center and RAINIER Steering Committee Co-Chair, who presented the data at ASN Kidney Week. “The results observed with povetacicept are among the most compelling I have seen in IgAN and highlight the potential of povetacicept to become an important new treatment option for patients living with this chronic progressive disease.”

Vertex also presented findings from a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on the device design and administration of current and emerging IgAN therapies, “Patient Perceptions of Injectable Therapies Among Adults with IgAN: A Qualitative Study” (#TH-PO0473). The study included in-depth, one-on-one interviews with 25 U.S. adults living with IgAN. Participants were shown pictures and short videos of the devices and asked to assess key treatment administration-related attributes. Findings showed that 96% of participants (24 of 25) preferred the characteristics of an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, citing features such as the needle not being visible and elimination of manual needle insertion. Additionally, 80% of patients (20 of 25) preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing, with the top reasons being convenience and travel or time away from home considerations.

Vertex also announced a new clinical trial underway for povetacicept:

  • PAVANT IgAN Patient Experience Study (NCT07890909), A Phase 3b, Open-label, Single-arm, Patient Experience Study of Povetacicept Injection (via Autoinjector) in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy

Visit news.vrtx.com/kidney-congress for more information about Vertex’s presence at ASN Kidney Week 2026.

Investor Event

Vertex will host an investor event and webcast on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT) in Denver, Colorado, to discuss the data for povetacicept in IgAN, the Company’s program in APOL1- mediated kidney disease (AMKD), and other highlights across its kidney disease portfolio.

A live webcast of the presentation and Q&A portions can be accessed through the Investor Relations section of Vertex's website at investors.vrtx.com. To ensure a timely connection, it is recommended that participants register at least 15 minutes prior to the scheduled webcast. An archived webcast will be available on the company's website in the “Investors” section.

About RAINIER

RAINIER (NCT06564142) is a global Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trial of povetacicept 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks versus placebo on top of standard of care in 605 adults with IgAN (N=557 in main cohort, N=48 in the exploratory cohort). The trial was designed to have a pre-planned interim analysis evaluating the percent change from baseline in UPCR for the povetacicept arm versus placebo after a pre-specified number of patients reach 36 weeks of treatment. Final analysis will occur at two years of treatment, with a primary endpoint of total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope through Week 104. RAINIER is the largest trial conducted in IgAN and achieved full enrollment faster than any contemporary IgAN trial.

As previously reported, patients treated with povetacicept achieved a 52.0% reduction from baseline in 24-hour UPCR at Week 36, with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction of 49.8% in 24-hour UPCR compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

The trial also met its secondary objective. For the first secondary endpoint, patients treated with povetacicept demonstrated a 77.4% reduction from baseline in serum galactose deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) compared to an increase of +9.1% in the placebo group, yielding a reduction of 79.3% compared to placebo (P<0.0001). For the second secondary endpoint, in patients with baseline hematuria, 85.1% achieved hematuria resolution in the povetacicept treatment group compared to 23.4% in the placebo group, resulting in hematuria resolution of 61.7% compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

Povetacicept was generally safe and well tolerated. The majority of adverse events (AEs) were mild to moderate. The most common events (≥10% of participants in either treatment group) for the povetacicept group versus the placebo group were upper respiratory tract infection (18.3% vs 11.4%), nasopharyngitis (9.7% vs 12.4%), and injection site reactions (14.5% vs 2.2%). There were no serious adverse events (SAEs) related to povetacicept and no deaths in the trial. There were no opportunistic infections, and no discontinuations due to infections. As expected, anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) were observed; these ADAs had no impact on efficacy or the risk profile.

Results from the RAINIER trial support the Biologics License Application (BLA) for povetacicept, which has been accepted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for accelerated approval in adults with IgAN. The Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date is November 30, 2026.

The RAINIER trial continues in a blinded manner until the last patient enrolled completes 104 weeks. Patients in RAINIER who have completed the Week 104 visit are eligible to enroll in the open-label extension study (NCT07807995), “A Phase 3 Open-Label Study of Long-term Treatment With Povetacicept in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy,” and receive an additional 104 weeks of treatment and follow-up.

About Povetacicept

Povetacicept is a dual inhibitor of the BAFF and APRIL cytokines, which promote B cell activation, differentiation and/or survival, and provides B cell control by inhibiting the ability of BAFF and APRIL to drive the pathogenesis of multiple immune-mediated diseases. Due to its engineered TACI domain, povetacicept has demonstrated improved binding affinity, potency, pharmacokinetics, and/or tissue distribution compared to other APRIL, BAFF, and dual BAFF+APRIL inhibitors in preclinical studies.

If povetacicept is approved by the FDA, Vertex plans to launch povetacicept as a low-volume (<0.5 mL) subcutaneous autoinjector delivered once every 4 weeks via at-home administration.

IgAN is the first of multiple indications that Vertex is exploring for povetacicept given its pipeline-in-a-product potential. There are ongoing studies including the Phase 2/3 OLYMPUS trial (NCT07204275) in primary membranous nephropathy (pMN) and the Phase 2 ETNA trial (NCT07501702) in generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).

About IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN is a serious, progressive, life-threatening kidney disease driven by uncontrolled autoreactive B cell activity and is the most common cause of primary glomerulonephritis, affecting approximately 330,000 people in the United States and Europe and more than 1.5 million globally. IgAN results from the deposition of circulating immune complexes, consisting of immunoglobulins and galactose-deficient immunoglobulin A (Gd-IgA1), in the renal glomerular mesangium, triggering kidney injury and fibrosis.

About Vertex

Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases and conditions. The company has approved therapies for cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, acute pain and acromegaly, and it continues to advance clinical and research programs in these areas. Vertex also has a robust clinical pipeline of investigational therapies across a range of modalities in other serious diseases where it has deep insight into causal human biology, including IgA nephropathy, neuropathic pain, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, primary membranous nephropathy, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent Cushing's syndrome, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, type 1 diabetes, generalized myasthenia gravis, and myotonic dystrophy type 1.

Vertex was founded in 1989 and has its global headquarters in Boston, with international headquarters in London. Additionally, the company has research and development sites and commercial offices in North America, Europe, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East. Vertex is consistently recognized as one of the industry's top places to work, including 17 consecutive years on Science magazine's Top Employers list and one of Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For. For company updates and to learn more about Vertex’s history of innovation, visit www.vrtx.com or follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and X.

Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements as defined in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended, including, without limitation, the statements made by Carmen Bozic, M.D., and Richard Lafayette, M.D., and statements regarding expectations for the potential accelerated approval of povetacicept in the U.S., expectations for new clinical trials planned for povetacicept, expectations for the RAINIER trial, expectations for the launch of povetacicept if approved by the FDA, expectations for the anticipated benefits of povetacicept, including its best-in-class potential, and the clinical status of and expectations for the Phase 2/3 OLYMPUS trial in pMN and the Phase 2 ETNA trial in gMG. While Vertex believes the forward-looking statements contained in this press release are accurate, these forward-looking statements represent the company's beliefs only as of the date of this press release and there are a number of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual events or results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such forward-looking statements. Those risks and uncertainties include, among other things, that data from the company’s clinical programs may not support registration or further development in a timely manner, or at all, due to safety, efficacy, and other risks, that the potential accelerated approval and/or the anticipated commercial launch of povetacicept may be delayed, if it occurs at all, and other risks listed under the heading “Risk Factors” in Vertex's most recent annual report and subsequent quarterly reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission at www.sec.gov and available through the company's website at www.vrtx.com. What Does Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s 6.35% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

What Does Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s 6.35% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

PR Newswire

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026

Suit alleges Anavex Life Sciences Corp. failed to disclose key facts to investors from November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026; lead plaintiff deadline is November 30, 2026

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith today reported that a securities class action lawsuit is pending against Anavex Life Sciences Corp. ("Anavex" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: AVXL) on behalf of investors who acquired its securities from November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026. The Anavex Life Sciences Corp. case, Kurey v. Anavex Life Sciences Corp. et al., was filed on September 29, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (Case No. 26-cv-08567).

Investors with losses on Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities can contact the Law Offices of Howard G. Smith about the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. lawsuit before the November 30, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

Key deadlines and dates for Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors

  • Lead plaintiff deadline: November 30, 2026
  • Class period: November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026
  • Complaint filed: September 29, 2026

What happened?

On May 11, 2026, the Company filed with the SEC a notification of late filing which disclosed it had "terminated the employment of Dr. Christopher Missling as the Chief Executive Officer of the Company on April 30, 2026 for, among other things, conduct that the Special Committee believed was inconsistent with Company Policy."

On this news, Anavex stock fell $0.18 per share, or 5.55%, to close at $3.06 on May 12, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Then, on August 28, 2026, Anavex filed an Amended 2025 Annual Report with the SEC. The report stated, in part, that as a result of a review by the Special Committee, management, in consultation with the Audit Committee of the Board, "concluded that there was a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting that existed at September 30, 2025" and that "the Company's disclosure controls and procedures were not effective."

On this news, Anavex stock fell $0.19 per share, or 6.35%, to close at $2.80 on August 31, 2026, thereby injuring investors further.

What is the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. lawsuit about?

The Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities lawsuit alleges that, between November 26, 2025 and August 28, 2026, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose that: (1) Anavex lacked adequate internal controls; (2) Anavex understated its potential regulatory challenges as a result of misconduct by former CEO Christopher Missling; and (3) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

"The lawsuit against Anavex Life Sciences Corp. alleges that, among other things, the Company failed to tell investors that Anavex lacked adequate internal controls. Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors who bought during the class period may be able to pursue their losses, and the November 30, 2026 deadline is where that process begins," said Howard G. Smith of The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith.

Next steps for Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors

Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors who suffered losses may contact The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to learn about pursuing their claims.

Lead plaintiff motions in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. class action are due to the Court by November 30, 2026. For more information, visit the firm's website, email howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, or call (215) 638-4847.

If you purchased Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities during the class period, you may retain counsel of your choice, or you may take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. case so far.

Common questions from Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors

Who is eligible? Investors who acquired Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities from November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026 and suffered losses may qualify for the class in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. shareholder lawsuit.

What is the deadline? Lead plaintiff motions in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. case are due by November 30, 2026.

Can I recover without being lead plaintiff? Yes, Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors may take no action and remain absent class members.

Does it cost anything? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith works on contingency, so investors pay no attorneys' fees unless there is a recovery, and any fees require court approval.

The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith has helped injured investors recover their money for more than 15 years. The firm prosecutes securities fraud, takeover, and derivative litigation against public companies and their officers, directors, and advisors in federal and state courts nationwide, and has helped clients recover hundreds of millions of dollars in losses. Clients speak directly with a lawyer, who will promptly answer any question.

data.title: New Poll: Voters Are Realizing This Income Tax Is Coming for Everyone
data.description:
New Poll: Voters Are Realizing This Income Tax Is Coming for Everyone

New Poll: Voters Are Realizing This Income Tax Is Coming for Everyone

PR Newswire

SEATTLE, Oct. 23, 2026

SEATTLE, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Recent real-time tracking poll shows Initiative 645 is very much in the fight. As voters learn that this really is an income tax coming for everyone, support for repeal rises to two-thirds. The results are consistent with several polls conducted earlier this year, both showing around 67% of voters oppose a state income tax. This latest survey, conducted by NMR Research with voters in Washington's 8th and 5th Congressional Districts, tested the official ballot language against a plain description of the tax. Districts like these, which provide a diverse cross-section of Washington voters, are where statewide majorities are won or lost.

"You can't cut money you don't have, and not a dime of this tax is collected until 2029. The ballot lets that lie stand, but voters know it's not true," said Jaime Herrera Beutler, spokesperson for Vote Yes Repeal the Income Tax. "These numbers show Washingtonians aren't fooled. They know this is an income tax designed to be expanded to working and fixed income families, and that it will capture every person, pension, and nonprofit in the state."

The Results

The survey of 188 voters in Congressional District 8 and 222 in District 5 was fielded Oct. 18-19 and has a margin of error of ±9.5 ±7 respectively. When voters surveyed were shown the official ballot language and statement in WA-8, they supported I-645 by 48% to 43%, with 9% undecided. When biased anti-repeal language was removed and voters were shown the truth, that this is an income tax, support for repeal rose to 67%, with 19% preferring to keep the tax and 14% undecided. In WA-5, voters supported I-645 by 46% to 43%, with 11% undecided. When that language was removed, support for repeal rose to 62%, with 20% preferring to keep the tax and 18% undecided. 

Model Districts Where Elections Are Won or Lost

These Districts are bellwether districts, covering over 7,300 square miles and nearly 800,000 residents across parts of King, Snohomish, Pierce, Kittitas, and Chelan counties, from suburban neighborhoods to Central Washington farmland. CD-5 covers Eastern Washington from Spokane to Walla Walla, with about 800,000 residents across ten counties and parts of two more. With District 8 leaning Democrat (D+3) and District 5 leaning Republican (R+5), these results suggest appeal for repealing the income tax reaches across party lines.

Voters can learn more at voteyes645.com. Ballots are in voters' hands now and are due Nov. 3.

The Capital Corporation Advises Champion Coach Inc. on Its Partnership With Hoffmann Family of Companies

The Capital Corporation (“TCC”, www.thecapitalcorp.com) is pleased to announce that it served as the exclusive investment banking advisor to Champion Coach, Inc. (“Champion Coach” or the “Company”) in its partnership with Hoffmann Family of Companies (“HF Companies”).

Headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina, Champion Coach is a leading provider of luxury motorcoach transportation services to professional sports teams, collegiate athletic programs, corporate groups, schools and universities, nonprofit organizations, and other customers throughout the United States. Founded by Craig and Hazel Dance in 1998, Champion Coach has built a nationally recognized reputation for providing safe, reliable, and high-quality transportation services, primarily within the sports end markets. Over nearly three decades, the Company has developed longstanding customer relationships and established a differentiated position in the luxury motorcoach transportation industry.

HF Companies is a family-owned investment organization that partners with established businesses across a diverse range of industries. Through its permanent-capital, long-term ownership model, HF Companies seeks to support continued growth while preserving the brands, cultures, employees, and leadership teams that have contributed to the success of its portfolio companies.

“The Hoffmann family shares our commitment to our customers, our employees, and the Champion Coach brand. Their resources and nationwide reach provide us a path to launch the Champion Coach brand across the country, providing attractive optionality for our customers,” said Craig Dance, Founder and CEO of Champion Coach.

The Capital Corporation conducted a targeted process designed to identify a partner that could support Champion Coach’s continued growth while remaining aligned with the Dances’ objectives regarding the Company’s employees, customers, culture, and long-term legacy.

“Champion Coach is an exceptional business with a highly regarded brand, a loyal customer base, and significant opportunities for continued growth,” said Devin Green, COO of The Capital Corporation. “From the outset of the process, Craig and Hazel were focused on finding a long-term partner that understood the standards and expectations that makes Champion Coach special and would preserve the legacy their family worked so hard to build. This partnership between Champion Coach and HF Companies creates a unique, strategic fit that is well positioned to unlock value for everyone involved. We were proud to advise the Dance family on this important transaction.”

The Company serves a diverse customer base that includes professional sports teams, collegiate athletic programs, corporate groups, schools and universities, nonprofit organizations, and other organizations requiring premium group transportation services. data.title: Novartis U.S. Shares Fall After MS Pill Trial Data Disappoint
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud 




  Novartis's U.S. shares fell after the Swiss drugmaker reported results of two late-stage studies of its multiple sclerosis pill that showed a reduction in flare-ups below that achieved by a rival drug from Roche Holding. 



  American depositary receipts in Novartis fell as much as 4.5% in U.S. midday trading Friday before recovering somewhat, reducing their year-to-date gains. 



  Novartis said its drug, known as remibrutinib and marketed as Rhapsido for skin condition chronic spontaneous urticaria, met the primary goals of the studies by reducing relapse rates relative to Sanofi's rival treatment Aubagio in patients with relapsing MS, the most common form of the disease. The results were presented at scientific congress MSToronto2026 in Toronto and published in medical journal the Lancet. 



  The studies showed the drug achieved reductions in the annualized relapse rate of 35.2% and 31.2% compared to Aubagio, the company said. This translated into one relapse every 13 years, it added. 



  No liver safety signal was observed, Novartis said. 



  Novartis, which was recently hit by trial failures of cholesterol and neuromuscular drugs, already reported initial findings from the studies last month, but analysts said a look at the full data was required to assess how its drug performed against the competitor product from Roche. 



  Roche, Novartis's Swiss cross-town rival, previously said its own multiple sclerosis pill, fenebrutinib, lowered the annualized relapse rate by 51.1% and 58.5% in two late-stage studies, but its drug showed signs of potential liver injury. 



  Analysts at UBS had said before Novartis released the full study data that the company would likely need to deliver efficacy data at least on par with Roche's fenebrutinib with a clean safety profile to trigger a positive market reaction. 



  Novartis said there were no cases that would raise concerns about drug-induced liver injury in its trials. Roche reported a case of potential liver damage. 



  By combining high efficacy with a favorable safety profile, the medicine has the potential to support long-term disease management, Novartis Chief Medical Officer Shreeram Aradhye said.

Deadline Alert: Bank Of America Corporation Investors Have Until December 15, 2026 to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role in Securities Fraud Class Action, Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Reminds Investors

Class action covers investors who bought Bank Of America Corporation securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026; complaint alleges the company failed to disclose material adverse facts

Investors in Bank Of America Corporation ("Bank of America" or the "Company") (NYSE: BAC) have until December 15, 2026 to ask the Court to appoint them lead plaintiff in a securities fraud class action lawsuit filed on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Bank Of America Corporation securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026, inclusive. Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP ("Glancy") today reminded investors of the upcoming deadline. The Bank Of America Corporation case, New England Teamsters Pension Fund v. Bank of America Corporation et al., was filed on October 16, 2026 and is pending in the U.S. District Court Southern District of New York (Case No. 1:26-cv-09137).

Investors who suffered losses on Bank Of America Corporation investments can contact Glancy about the Bank Of America Corporation class action to learn about potentially pursuing claims under the federal securities laws before the December 15, 2026 deadline.

Deadline and key dates for Bank Of America Corporation investors

  • Lead plaintiff deadline: December 15, 2026
  • Class period: August 1, 2025 to October 13, 2026, inclusive
  • Complaint filed: October 16, 2026
  • Court: U.S. District Court Southern District of New York

What happened?

On October 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced a $1.2 billion fine against Bank of America Corporation for violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws. According to the Department of the Treasury, Bank of America Corporation failed to mitigate and report priority national security risks. The Department of the Treasury also found that the Company’s Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money laundering compliance programs were deficient and ineffective.

On this news, Bank of America stock fell $2.57 or, 4.76%, to close at $51.39 on October 14, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

What does the Bank Of America Corporation complaint allege?

The Bank Of America Corporation securities lawsuit alleges that, throughout the class period, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Bank Of America Corporation's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) systemic weaknesses in BANA's BSA/AML program caused it to fail to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and to miss, delay, or file inaccurate or incomplete suspicious activity reports involving billions of dollars in suspicious activity; (2) internal reports had documented BANA's BSA/AML deficiencies for years, yet BANA had not adequately remedied them after the 2024 Consent Order; (3) BANA also had deficiencies in its sanctions compliance program and processed transactions later identified as apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs; (4) fixing these deficiencies required significant additional compliance resources and exposed BANA to substantial penalties and costs; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Bank Of America Corporation's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Bank Of America Corporation securities during the class period may move the Court no later than December 15, 2026 to request appointment as lead plaintiff in this putative class action lawsuit.

"The complaint against Bank Of America Corporation alleges, among other things, that the Company failed to disclose that systemic weaknesses in BANA's BSA/AML program caused it to fail to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and to miss, delay, or file inaccurate or incomplete suspicious activity reports involving billions of dollars in suspicious activity. The December 15, 2026 deadline to request appointment as lead plaintiff is approaching, and investors considering that role should act promptly," said Charles H. Linehan, Partner at Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP.

What's the next step?

Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP is a leading national shareholder rights law firm that can help Bank Of America Corporation investors evaluate potential claims to recover their losses. Investors who wish to serve as lead plaintiff in the Bank Of America Corporation class action must move the Court by December 15, 2026. To learn more, visit the Bank Of America Corporation case page, email shareholders@glancylaw.com, or call 310-201-9150 (toll-free: 888-773-9224).

If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.

To be a member of the Bank Of America Corporation class, you need not take any action at this time. You may retain counsel of your choice or take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified yet in the Bank Of America Corporation case.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible? Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Bank Of America Corporation securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 and suffered losses may be members of the proposed class in the Bank Of America Corporation shareholder lawsuit.

When is the Bank Of America Corporation lead plaintiff deadline? Motions to serve as lead plaintiff in the Bank Of America Corporation class action must be filed with the U.S. District Court Southern District of New York by December 15, 2026.

What if I miss the Bank Of America Corporation deadline? After December 15, 2026, investors generally can no longer ask to be appointed lead plaintiff, but Bank Of America Corporation investors may still remain class members. Their ability to share in any future recovery does not depend on serving as lead plaintiff.

What is a lead plaintiff? In the Bank Of America Corporation class action, the lead plaintiff is the investor, or group of investors, that the court appoints to represent all class members and oversee the case. Under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act, courts generally presume the movant with the largest financial interest is the most adequate lead plaintiff.

Does it cost anything to contact Glancy or participate in this action? Glancy represents Bank Of America Corporation investors on a contingency fee basis, so investors pay no attorneys' fees out of pocket. Any attorneys' fees and litigation expenses are paid only from a recovery, if one is obtained, and are subject to court approval.

Why work with Glancy on the Bank Of America Corporation lawsuit? Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP is a premier law firm with decades of experience representing investors and consumers in securities litigation and other complex class action litigation. Contact Glancy about the Bank Of America Corporation class action. Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

About Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP

Glancy was named one of Law360's Securities Groups of the Year and ranked second in total investor recoveries by ISS Securities Class Action Services in 2025.

Glancy's successes have been widely covered by leading news and industry publications, including The Wall Street Journal, The Financial Times, Bloomberg Businessweek, Reuters, the Associated Press, Barron's, Investor's Business Daily, Forbes, and Money.

Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

Deadline Alert: Millrose Properties, Inc. Stockholders Face December 8, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline in Securities Fraud Class Action, The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Highlights

Class action on behalf of investors who bought Millrose Properties, Inc. securities from February 7, 2025 through October 2, 2026 alleges the company failed to disclose key facts

Millrose Properties, Inc. ("Millrose" or the "Company") (NYSE: MRP) investors who wish to serve as lead plaintiff in a pending securities fraud class action lawsuit must move the Court by December 8, 2026. The suit was filed on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired the Company's securities from February 7, 2025 through October 2, 2026, inclusive. The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith today highlighted the deadline in the case, Rubenstsein et al. v. Millrose Properties, Inc. et al., which was filed on October 9, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida (Case No. 9:26-cv-81386).

Investors with losses on Millrose Properties, Inc. securities can reach The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith about the Millrose Properties, Inc. lawsuit before the December 8, 2026 deadline to discuss potential claims under the federal securities laws.

Key deadline for Millrose Properties, Inc. investors

  • Deadline for lead plaintiff motions: December 8, 2026
  • Class period: February 7, 2025 through October 2, 2026, inclusive
  • Complaint filing date: October 9, 2026
  • Court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida

What happened?

On October 2, 2026, Hunterbrook published a report alleging that “[c]ontrary to the plans in its initial SEC filings, Millrose has now bought an estimated $200 million of Lennar homes in about a month and is renting them out at what appears to be a loss.” Further, the report stated that although “[a]ccounting rules say a company cannot book a sale to an entity it controls; a forensic accountant told Hunterbrook the question of Lennar’s control over Millrose seems ‘black and white’ in spirit[.”]

On this news, Millrose stock fell $2.10 per share, or 8.53%, to close at $22.51 on October 5, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Allegations in the Millrose Properties, Inc. case

The Millrose Properties, Inc. shareholder lawsuit alleges that, throughout the class period, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Millrose Properties, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) despite representations to the contrary, Millrose's objectives were not limited to engaging in land purchases, horizontal development, and homesite option purchase arrangements for Lennar and potentially other homebuilders and developers; (2) despite representations to the contrary, Millrose would in fact enter into lease agreements and would have tenants in its properties; (3) Millrose would purchase $200 million worth of properties from Lennar; (4) Millrose would lease the properties purchased from Lennar out at a loss; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Millrose Properties, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Millrose Properties, Inc. investors who purchased or otherwise acquired securities during the class period may move the Court by December 8, 2026 to seek appointment as lead plaintiff in this putative class action.

"The lawsuit against Millrose Properties, Inc. alleges that, among other things, the Company failed to tell investors that despite representations to the contrary, Millrose's objectives were not limited to engaging in land purchases, horizontal development, and homesite option purchase arrangements for Lennar and potentially other homebuilders and developers. Millrose Properties, Inc. investors who bought during the class period may want to know their options before the December 8, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline passes," said Howard G. Smith of The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith.

Next steps for Millrose Properties, Inc. investors

Millrose Properties, Inc. investors who suffered losses may contact The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to learn about pursuing their claims. Lead plaintiff motions in the Millrose Properties, Inc. class action are due to the Court by December 8, 2026. For more information, visit the firm's website, email howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, or call (215) 638-4847.

To be a member of the Millrose Properties, Inc. class, you need not take any action at this time; you may retain counsel of your choice or take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified so far in the Millrose Properties, Inc. case.

Common questions from Millrose Properties, Inc. investors

Who is eligible? Investors who acquired Millrose Properties, Inc. securities from February 7, 2025 through October 2, 2026 and suffered losses may qualify for the class in the Millrose Properties, Inc. shareholder lawsuit.

What is the deadline? Lead plaintiff motions in the Millrose Properties, Inc. case are due by December 8, 2026.

data.title: PureTalk Customers Help Raise More Than $1 Million For Veterans
data.description:
COVINGTON, GA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / PureTalk, the Veteran-led wireless company known for offering premium wireless service at a fraction of the cost of major carriers, today announced it has raised more than $1 million for America's Warrior Partnership (AWP), a national nonprofit that connects Veterans and their families with supportive community resources and services to help improve and save Veterans' lives. The total combines monthly roundups where customers round their bill up to the nearest dollar, one-time customer donations and company matching campaigns, including a recent PureTalk match of $250,000 during the company's America250 campaign this summer. Every donated dollar goes to AWP and its programs

"Building a community network to recognize and support the unique needs of Veterans and their families is at the heart of the American's Warrior Partnership mission," said Jim Lorraine, president and CEO of America's Warrior Partnership. "PureTalk takes that concept and puts it into action. We are grateful for PureTalk's partnership and their leading a groundswell of meaningful community support among their customers to measurably improve the lives of Veterans and their loved ones."

"My dad gets his care from the VA, so the Deeds Not Words initiative is personal," said William Curry, Chief Strategy Officer at Telrite Holdings. "We have Veterans to thank for ensuring America's way of life. We want to help ensure theirs."

"Veterans need a hand up, not a handout," said Clint Romesha, Medal of Honor recipient and AWP board member Emeritus. "Since 2023, PureTalk and America's Warrior Partnership have been working to give Veterans the support they need; we've raised over $1 million in that effort," he continued. "That's the definition of Deeds Not Words, right there."

Marine Corps Veteran David Bennett received mortgage assistance that kept his family in their home after his wife unexpectedly lost her job.

"Me and my family fell on some hard times, and we didn't know if we'd be able to keep our home," Bennett said.

Army Reserve Veteran Dale Dyer was recovering from a serious injury that kept him out of work when the family's vehicle broke down. AWP and PureTalk covered the repair so he could return to work.

The support continues. New PureTalk customers can start a monthly round-up or make a one-time donation when they sign up for PureTalk wireless service, or existing customers can donate through their online account. Details are available at PureTalk.com/roundup.

About PureTalk

PureTalk, a subsidiary of Telrite Holdings, Inc., is a Veteran-led wireless provider that offers superior wireless plans backed by a dependable nationwide 5G network at a fraction of the cost of major carriers. With 100% U.S.-based operations, including customer service, PureTalk built its reputation on honesty, integrity, and delivering real value to its customers. PureTalk is committed to supporting hardworking Americans and the military members who serve our country. Together with its customers, PureTalk has contributed more than $1 million to America's Warrior Partnership and helped eliminate $10 million in veteran debt. It supports K9s For Warriors, mikeroweWORKS Foundation, and other organizations that help Veterans and their families. For more information, visit PureTalk.com.

About America's Warrior Partnership

America's Warrior Partnership is a national 501(c)(3) nonprofit that connects Veterans, their families and caregivers with resources, services and partnerships in their own communities. AWP works through its community integration model, the AWP Network and research initiatives that include Operation Deep Dive, a multi-year study of Veteran suicide and other non-natural deaths. Learn more at americaswarriorpartnership.org.
